lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- What I Do -- Explaining Your Job
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 13 -- What I Do

listenings.text: Hi everyone, my name is Laura Chen, and I run the water department of a city utility in Arizona. My team supplies water to almost a million people, in one of the driest places in the country. What do I do all day? I do not design anything anymore. I oversee three engineers and a lab, and I spend most of my time with stakeholders: the city council, the farmers and the public. The hardest part of my job is not the engineering. It is explaining the engineering to people who do not care about pipes, until the day the water stops.

People always ask me what a consultant actually does, so here is my week. On Monday, my team reviews the data from the treatment plant. On Tuesday and Wednesday, I write the report, because every project has a deliverable, and the client expects it on Friday. On Thursday, I usually visit the site, which is the best part of the job. And on Friday, I present the numbers to the client. My wife says my job is simple: I tell people how much their water costs. She is not completely wrong.

extra_audio.text: First, the water utility hires the consultancy for a study. Then, the team studies the sewage network and collects the data. After that, the engineers design the treatment plant. Next, every month, a deliverable goes to the client. Finally, the stakeholders give their opinion and the client decides.

items.situation: Somebody at a conference asks what your company does.
tips: The company is it: the verb takes -s.
Use consultancy and advice or design.

items.situation: A new colleague asks who your usual client is.
tips: Say what kind of company it is.
Explain what it does in one sentence, with -ies.

items.situation: Explain what your manager does on a project.
tips: There is one verb for watching and controlling the work.
He or she, so the verb takes -s.

items.situation: A friend outside engineering asks what happens at a treatment plant.
tips: Start with what comes in: sewage.
The plant ... the water. Remember the -s.

items.situation: Your client asks when the next document arrives.
tips: There is one word for the document you owe the client.
